name: plan-guardian
description: Plan review workflow plugin with a plan-reviewer agent for rigorous plan quality checks. Non-blocking by default — Claude autonomously decides when to review, or users can trigger manually via /plan-review. v1.3.0 adds an opt-out codex review gate: a PreToolUse:ExitPlanMode hook intercepts plan-mode exits, instructs Claude to run /plan-guardian:codex-plan-review which loops `codex exec` against the plan and revises it until Codex emits NO_CONCERNS; set CODEX_PLAN_REVIEW=0 to disable. v1.4.x consolidated the loop's writes into a pre-approvable plan-review-helper.sh + a /plan-guardian:setup command of scoped allow-rules. v1.5.0 replaces the on-disk sha256 sentinel with an INLINE review marker carried inside the plan text: on convergence the loop appends `<!-- codex-reviewed:<token> -->` as the plan's last line, and the hook validates that token (a CODEX_REVIEW_SECRET-keyed sha256 of the plan body, or a literal fallback when unset). The loop now writes NOTHING to disk during plan mode — the proof rides through tool_input.plan — which sidesteps the upstream bug where the allow-list intermittently fails to suppress Write/Edit prompts under mode toggles. plan-review-helper.sh is reduced to one shared `digest` subcommand used by both mint (command) and verify (hook); /plan-guardian:setup now needs only the two Bash allow-rules (codex exec + helper), not Write/Edit. v1.5.1 makes content-binding the default: the helper resolves the signing key as CODEX_REVIEW_SECRET if set, else a per-machine auto key file (~/.claude/plan-guardian/secret, mode 600, generated on first use), else the literal fallback only when no key can be established — so every user gets the content-bound marker with no setup.
